title: Partial Label Learning with Discrimination Augmentation

problem.claim: Partial label learning must disambiguate multiple candidate labels to identify the valid label for each training example.

gap.claim: Existing approaches focus mainly on output-space disambiguation, while less informative feature representations may negatively affect the disambiguation process.

contributions.claim: The paper investigates discrimination augmentation for partial label learning by enriching the feature space with confidence-rated class prototype features.
It proposes an optimization formulation that jointly optimizes class prototypes and estimates labeling confidence, enforcing global feature-space consistency and local label-space consistency.
The class prototypes and labeling confidence are solved via alternating optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents the first attempt toward discrimination augmentation for partial label learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world data sets validate the effectiveness of the approach for improving the generalization performance of state-of-the-art partial label learning algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Partial label learning uses multiple candidate labels per example, with only one valid label.
Existing work mainly performs candidate-label disambiguation in the output space.
Less informative feature representations can impair disambiguation.
The approach augments features with confidence-rated class prototypes and jointly optimizes prototypes and labeling confidence.
The authors report alternating optimization and experiments on synthetic and real-world data sets showing improved generalization performance.
